nodes.title: Arrays & hashing
nodes.description: Turn repeated scans into small, reusable summaries.
nodes.approach: Choose what information each prefix must preserve: membership, counts, positions, or a cumulative value.
tips: Check duplicates and negative values.
Decide whether order matters before sorting.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Lookup & counting
nodes.description: Remember exactly what later elements need.
nodes.approach: Use a hash map to answer a previously linear query in expected constant time.
tips: Check before inserting when an element must not match itself.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Complement lookup
nodes.description: A pair must add to a target.
nodes.approach: For each value x, look for target − x among earlier values. Store indices only after the lookup.
tips: Inserting first can reuse the same index.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Frequency signatures
nodes.description: Group items that differ only by ordering.
nodes.approach: Use the sorted characters as a stable signature and collect equal signatures together.
tips: A set loses multiplicity: abb and ab are different.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

pseudocode.code:
groups ← empty map

for each word in words:
    letters ← sort(characters(word))
    signature ← join(letters)

    if signature is not in groups:
        groups[signature] ← empty list

    append word to groups[signature]

return all lists stored in groups
pseudocode.example:
"eat" → "aet" → ["eat"]
"tea" → "aet" → ["eat", "tea"]
"abb" → "abb" → ["abb"]
"ab"  → "ab"  → ["ab"]

Same signature → same group.
Repeated letters stay in the signature.

nodes.title: Sequence boundary detection
nodes.description: Find a consecutive run in unsorted data.
nodes.approach: Only grow a run from x when x−1 is absent. Each distinct value is visited within one run.
tips: Starting a walk from every value produces quadratic work.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Prefix & difference
nodes.description: Exchange repeated range work for cumulative state.
nodes.approach: Define a prefix at an exclusive boundary; obtain a range by subtracting two prefixes.
tips: Seed the empty prefix.
Difference arrays invert the direction: record changes, then accumulate.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Prefix sum with frequency map
nodes.description: Count subarrays with a given sum, including negative values.
nodes.approach: A subarray ending at this prefix has sum k when an earlier prefix equals current−k. Count earlier prefixes before adding the current one.
tips: A sliding window is not monotone when negative values are allowed.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Remainder classes
nodes.description: A range sum must be divisible by k.
nodes.approach: Two prefix sums with the same remainder differ by a multiple of k.

nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Prefix and suffix products
nodes.description: Each answer excludes exactly one element.
nodes.approach: Write left products into the output, then multiply by a running right product.
tips: Division breaks when zeros appear.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Range updates with differences
nodes.description: Many intervals add an amount to every covered position.
nodes.approach: Add at the start and subtract immediately after the end, then take a prefix sum once.

nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Two-dimensional prefix sums

nodes.title: In-place structure

nodes.title: Index placement
nodes.description: Values map naturally to positions 1 through n.
nodes.approach: Repeatedly place each in-range value x at index x−1. The first mismatch identifies the missing positive.
tips: Check the destination value to avoid infinite swaps with duplicates.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Boyer–Moore cancellation
nodes.description: One value is guaranteed to occupy more than half the positions.
nodes.approach: Cancel unequal pairs; the strict majority survives as the candidate.
tips: Without the majority guarantee, verify the candidate in a second pass.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Matrix boundary simulation
nodes.description: Visit a matrix in concentric rectangular layers.
nodes.approach: Maintain four unvisited boundaries; consume the top, right, bottom, then left side.
tips: Recheck boundaries before the bottom and left passes on thin matrices.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Two pointers & windows
nodes.description: Make a pair of boundaries do the work of nested loops.
nodes.approach: Find a monotone reason to advance one boundary without missing an answer.
tips: Write what makes a window valid.
Distinguish maximizing a valid window from minimizing a covering window.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Opposing & forward pointers
nodes.description: Exploit sorted order or independent read/write positions.
nodes.approach: Eliminate a candidate region with each movement.
tips: Prove why moving one pointer cannot discard a better answer.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Opposing pointers on sorted values
nodes.description: A sorted pair must meet a target.
nodes.approach: When the sum is too small, increase the left value; when too large, decrease the right value.
tips: This monotonic argument requires sorted input.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Fix one, solve two-sum

nodes.approach: Sort, fix the first value, then solve two-sum on the suffix; skip equal values at each decision boundary.

nodes.title: Move the limiting boundary
nodes.description: Area depends on width and the shorter endpoint.
nodes.approach: The shorter wall limits the area. Holding it while narrowing the interval cannot improve the answer, so move it.
tips: Moving the taller wall has no such elimination guarantee.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Read/write compaction
nodes.description: Keep selected elements in order, in place.
nodes.approach: Write each nonzero element into the next kept position, then fill the suffix with zeros.

nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Three-way partition
nodes.description: Separate three value classes in one pass.
nodes.approach: Maintain [0,low) as zeros, [low,mid) as ones, and (high,n) as twos. Classify the unknown at mid.
tips: After swapping with high, the new mid value is still unclassified.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Sliding windows
nodes.description: Reuse the work shared by adjacent contiguous ranges.
nodes.approach: Expand the right boundary, update summary state, and shrink from the left according to validity.
tips: Each element should enter and leave at most once.
Use prefix sums instead if validity is not monotone.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Fixed-length rolling window
nodes.description: Optimize over all contiguous ranges of exactly k elements.
nodes.approach: Start with one complete window; each shift adds the entering value and removes the departing value.

nodes.title: Longest valid window
nodes.description: Find the longest range without duplicate symbols.

nodes.approach: Perform stable counting passes from least significant to most significant digit, then inspect adjacent gaps.
tips: Every pass must be stable to preserve the previous digit order.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

nodes.title: Bits, math & geometry
nodes.description: Exploit representation, arithmetic structure, and geometric invariants.
nodes.approach: Translate operations into algebra before selecting an implementation.
tips: Watch overflow in fixed-width languages.
State the random distribution or numeric precision assumptions.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Bit representations
nodes.description: Treat an integer as a compact set of boolean choices.
nodes.approach: Use XOR for parity, AND for intersection, and shifts to address individual bits.
tips: Python integers are unbounded; negative bit behavior differs from fixed-width words.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: XOR cancellation
nodes.description: All values occur twice except one.
nodes.approach: Equal values cancel under XOR and zero is the identity, leaving the odd-occurrence value.
tips: This rule depends on the exact multiplicity guarantee.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Remove the lowest set bit
nodes.description: Count set bits without scanning zero bits.
nodes.approach: n & (n−1) removes the least significant set bit; repeat until the number becomes zero.
tips: This loop assumes a nonnegative fixed-width input.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Common binary prefix
nodes.description: AND every number in a contiguous integer range.
nodes.approach: Shift both boundaries until they match; all lower differing bits vanish somewhere in the range.
tips: Do not iterate through the entire numeric range.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Distinct suffix-OR compression
nodes.description: All suffix ORs change only when a new bit appears.
nodes.approach: Maintain the distinct OR values of subarrays ending here; OR each previous value with x and include x itself.
tips: The number of distinct states is bounded by bit width, not array length.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Number theory & counting
nodes.description: Use divisibility and combinatorial structure to shrink the search.
nodes.approach: Reduce by gcd, factor repeated contributions, or count equivalent outcomes instead of enumerating them.
tips: Use modular arithmetic throughout large counting recurrences.
nodes.why: Master these building blocks before combining them with other techniques.

nodes.title: Euclidean gcd structure
nodes.description: A common repeating block must divide both lengths.
nodes.approach: If concatenating in either order gives the same string, the gcd-length prefix is the largest common block.
tips: Compatible lengths alone do not prove compatible content.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 一、数论 / §1.6 最大公约数（GCD）

nodes.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
nodes.description: Find many primes below a bound.
nodes.approach: Mark multiples of each prime starting at its square; smaller multiples already have a smaller prime factor.
tips: The problem asks for primes strictly below n.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

references.title: 一、数论 / §1.2 预处理质数（筛质数）

nodes.title: Exponentiation by squaring
nodes.description: Compute a large power with logarithmically many multiplications.
nodes.approach: Square the base each step and multiply it into the result when the current exponent bit is set.
tips: Invert the base once for negative exponents.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Prime valuation in factorials
nodes.description: Count trailing zeroes without computing a factorial.
nodes.approach: Each zero needs factors 2 and 5; twos are abundant, so count multiples of 5, 25, 125, and so on.
tips: Multiples of 25 contribute more than one factor of five.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 一、数论 / §1.4 阶乘分解

nodes.title: Catalan decomposition
nodes.description: A root independently splits ordered keys into left and right substructures.
nodes.approach: Sum leftCount × rightCount across each possible root split.
tips: An empty subtree has one possible structure.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Geometry & randomness
nodes.description: Use exact invariants for geometry and explicit distributions for sampling.
nodes.approach: Prefer integer cross products for orientation and cumulative counts for weighted random choices.
tips: Avoid floating-point slopes for collinearity.
nodes.why: Learn this family after the core patterns to handle more specialized constraints.

nodes.title: Normalized slope counting
nodes.description: Find the largest collinear set.
nodes.approach: Fix an anchor and group other points by reduced (dx,dy), using gcd and a consistent sign convention.
tips: Vertical and horizontal lines need the same normalization discipline.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Reservoir sampling
nodes.description: Uniformly select one matching position from an unknown-length stream.
nodes.approach: On the kth matching occurrence, replace the selected index with probability 1/k. Each prior choice survives with the complementary probability.
tips: Choosing the first match or sampling values instead of indices is biased.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 六、随机算法 / §6.1 随机数

nodes.title: Weighted prefix sampling
nodes.description: Select an index with probability proportional to a positive weight.
nodes.approach: Build cumulative weights, draw an integer from 1 through total, then find the first cumulative weight at least that integer.
tips: Use inclusive integer bounds consistently to avoid off-by-one bias.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 六、随机算法 / §6.1 随机数

nodes.title: Grouped prefix choices
nodes.description: Choose a prefix from each pile under a total item budget.
nodes.approach: For each pile, precompute prefix values and try taking 0..min(pileSize,budget) items from the previous layer.
tips: Reading from the new layer would let one pile be selected more than once.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 三、背包 / §3.4 分组背包

nodes.title: Bounded multiplicity counting
nodes.description: Each choice can be used a limited number of times.
nodes.approach: Process one item type per layer and enumerate its allowed count without exceeding the target.
tips: Treat identical questions of one type as indistinguishable choices.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 三、背包 / §3.3 多重背包（选做）

nodes.title: Subset partition with remainder
nodes.description: Partition a small set into equal-sum groups.
nodes.approach: For each used-item mask, store the filled amount in the current bucket modulo target; completed buckets reset the remainder.
tips: The total sum must divide k, and no item may exceed the bucket target.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 九、状态压缩 DP（状压 DP） / §9.7 其他状压 DP

nodes.title: Visited-set shortest walk
nodes.description: The future depends on current position and all visited vertices.
nodes.approach: Run multi-source BFS over (vertex,visitedMask), starting once at each possible first vertex.
tips: Revisiting a vertex with a different mask is a different state.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 九、状态压缩 DP（状压 DP） / §9.3 旅行商问题（TSP）

nodes.title: SOS subset aggregation
nodes.description: Count compatible bitmasks across many subsets.
nodes.approach: Count all pairwise AND results, apply a subset-sum transform, then query masks contained in the complement of each third value.
tips: Complement only the relevant bit width, not Python’s unbounded complement.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

nodes.title: Two simultaneous walkers
nodes.description: Two agents collect values on the same row without double-counting.
nodes.approach: Use (row,col1,col2) as state; try the nine pairs of next-column moves, counting a shared cell once.
tips: Separate single-agent optimum paths may overlap and produce a wrong combined answer.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 二、网格图 DP / §2.2 进阶

nodes.title: Minimum-cut palindrome partition
nodes.description: Minimize how many valid pieces cover a sequence.
nodes.approach: Precompute palindrome intervals while considering endpoints; each palindromic suffix extends an optimal partition of the preceding prefix.
tips: The empty-prefix cut count is −1 so a whole-string palindrome uses zero cuts.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 五、划分型 DP / §5.2 最优划分

nodes.title: Digit DP with uniqueness mask
nodes.description: Count bounded integers with no repeated digit.
nodes.approach: Track position, tightness, and a used-digit mask. A zero mask also represents not having started, so leading zeroes consume no digit.
tips: Exclude the all-leading-zero construction from positive-integer counts.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 十、数位 DP / §10.1 统计合法元素的数目

nodes.title: Prefix-sum transition optimization
nodes.description: A recurrence sums a sliding interval of previous states.
nodes.approach: Insert the largest value into a permutation: it adds 0..size−1 inversions. Maintain a rolling sum over the previous row’s relevant interval.
tips: Subtract the value leaving the transition window before taking modulo.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 十一、优化 DP / §11.1 前缀和优化 DP

nodes.title: Matrix exponentiation of transitions
nodes.description: Apply the same linear transition an enormous number of times.
nodes.approach: Represent the recurrence by a fixed matrix and exponentiate it by squaring.
tips: Matrix multiplication order matters even though powers of the same matrix commute.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 十一、优化 DP / §11.6 矩阵快速幂优化 DP

nodes.title: Shortest signed-sum window with deque
nodes.description: Negative values invalidate the usual shrinking-window argument.
nodes.approach: Use prefix sums and keep increasing prefix values in a deque. Pop front when the target is reached and pop back when a later prefix dominates an earlier one.
tips: Store the empty prefix at index zero.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Count valid window suffixes
nodes.description: Count all subarrays satisfying a monotone positive-product bound.
nodes.approach: After shrinking to a valid window, every suffix ending at right is also valid, contributing right−left+1.
tips: The argument requires positive integers; k≤1 has no answers.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

references.title: 二、不定长滑动窗口 / §2.3 求子数组个数 / §2.3.1 越短越合法

nodes.title: Two sorted interval streams
nodes.description: Intersect two internally disjoint ordered interval lists.
nodes.approach: Emit the overlap when max(starts)≤min(ends), then advance whichever interval ends first.
tips: Advance by end time, not by start time.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 四、双序列双指针 / §4.1 双指针

nodes.title: Grouped run scanning
nodes.description: Process maximal consecutive runs of equal values.
nodes.approach: Move a right pointer to the end of one run, process it once, then begin at that boundary.
tips: Be sure to process the final run.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Kth value via cumulative counts
nodes.description: Find the kth smallest value in a row- and column-sorted matrix.
nodes.approach: Binary search a value and count how many entries are at most it with a staircase scan.
tips: Duplicates each contribute separately to the rank.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 二、二分答案 / §2.6 第 K 小/大

nodes.title: Weighted union-find potentials
nodes.description: Maintain multiplicative relations between variables.
nodes.approach: Store weight[x]=x/parent[x]. Path compression multiplies weights; merging roots derives a ratio between representatives.
tips: Unknown variables remain unknown even in x/x queries.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Kruskal edge selection
nodes.description: Build a minimum spanning tree by globally cheapest edges.
nodes.approach: Sort all edges and accept an edge only if it joins two different union-find components.
tips: Do not accept edges that close a cycle.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 四、最小生成树

nodes.title: Strongly connected component condensation
nodes.description: Separate directed cycles from the acyclic graph between them.
nodes.approach: Use Tarjan’s active-stack low-link algorithm to identify SCCs, mark cyclic SCCs, then propagate unsafety backward through the condensation graph.
tips: An edge to a finished SCC must not lower the current low-link value.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 一、图的遍历 / §1.1 深度优先搜索（DFS）
二、拓扑排序 / §2.1 拓扑排序

nodes.title: Bipartite matching by augmenting paths
nodes.description: Assign distinct compatible partners to maximize matched pairs.
nodes.approach: For each left vertex, search for a free right vertex or reroute its current match. Each successful augment increases matching size by one.
tips: Reset visited right vertices for each augmentation attempt.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 八、网络流

nodes.title: Lazy segment tree range flips
nodes.description: Many range updates affect an aggregate without touching every element.
nodes.approach: Store the count of ones per segment and a lazy flip bit. Flipping changes ones to segmentLength−ones; two flips cancel.
tips: Push pending flips before descending into a partially covered segment.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 八、树状数组和线段树 / §8.4 Lazy 线段树（有区间更新）

nodes.title: Dynamic sparse segment tree
nodes.description: The coordinate domain is huge but only a few intervals are updated.
nodes.approach: Allocate segment nodes only when traversed; store a local lazy increment plus the maximum of child contributions.
tips: Half-open bookings [start,end) become inclusive [start,end−1] for the tree.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 二、差分 / §2.1 一维差分 / §2.1.2 进阶
八、树状数组和线段树 / §8.5 动态开点线段树

nodes.title: Sparse table idempotent queries
nodes.description: The array is static and many overlapping min/max queries are needed.
nodes.approach: Precompute extrema for powers of two. Two possibly overlapping blocks cover each range because max is idempotent.
tips: This overlapping-block trick does not work for sums.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 四、队列 / §4.4 单调队列

nodes.title: Square-root decomposition
nodes.description: Trade simpler implementation for square-root range operations.
nodes.approach: Keep raw values plus block sums. Consume boundary elements individually and full interior blocks by summary.
tips: Update the block by the assignment delta.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 八、树状数组和线段树 / §8.1 树状数组
十、根号算法 / §10.1 分块

nodes.title: Offline sorted-threshold connectivity
nodes.description: Many connectivity queries permit edges only below a changing threshold.
nodes.approach: Sort edges and queries by limit. Incrementally union newly permitted edges, answering queries in that order and restoring output order.
tips: The threshold is strict: an edge equal to limit is excluded.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 九、其他

nodes.title: Suffix array and adjacent LCP
nodes.description: Find the longest repeated substring, allowing overlaps.
nodes.approach: Sort suffixes by doubling ranked prefixes. The largest common prefix of adjacent suffixes is the longest repeat; compute LCPs using Kasai’s reuse invariant.
tips: Avoid constructing all suffix strings, which uses quadratic space.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 四、字符串哈希
八、后缀数组/后缀自动机

nodes.title: Aho–Corasick multi-pattern matching
nodes.description: Many dictionary words must be matched during one text scan.
nodes.approach: Build trie failure links to the longest suffix that is also a trie prefix. Each terminal match offers a word-break DP transition.
tips: Failure links must carry terminal outputs from suffix states.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

nodes.title: Minimal cyclic rotation
nodes.description: Choose the lexicographically smallest rotation.
nodes.approach: For k=1 only rotations are reachable: compare two candidate starts and skip dominated starts after a mismatch. With k>1, arbitrary sorting is reachable.
tips: A mismatch eliminates an entire range of starts, making the rotation scan linear.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 五、最小表示法

nodes.title: Convex hull with cross products
nodes.description: Find the boundary of a point set.
nodes.approach: Build lower and upper monotone chains, popping turns that bend inward. Keep collinear boundary points by popping only strictly wrong turns.
tips: The strictness differs when only extreme hull vertices are wanted.
nodes.why: Useful when tighter constraints defeat the standard approach. Learn the prerequisites first.

references.title: 五、计算几何 / §5.4 凸包

nodes.title: Inclusion–exclusion with LCM
nodes.description: Count numbers divisible by at least one of several factors.
nodes.approach: Add single-factor counts, subtract pair intersections, and add the triple intersection. Binary search the first value whose union count reaches n.
tips: Intersections use LCM, not the product when factors overlap.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 二、组合数学 / §2.3 容斥原理

nodes.title: Rejection sampling without modulo bias
nodes.description: Create a uniform target range from a different uniform source.
nodes.approach: Two independent rand7 calls create 49 equally likely outcomes. Accept the first 40 and map them into ten equal buckets.
tips: Taking modulo ten across all 49 outcomes is biased.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 六、随机算法 / §6.1 随机数

nodes.title: Fisher–Yates shuffle
nodes.description: Generate each permutation with equal probability.
nodes.approach: At position i from the end, swap with a uniformly chosen position in [0,i]. Fix that position permanently.
tips: Sampling from the full array at every step produces a biased shuffle.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 六、随机算法 / §6.1 随机数

nodes.title: Random access with swap-delete
nodes.description: Support insert, remove, and random selection in expected constant time.
nodes.approach: Combine an array with value-to-index lookup. Delete by moving the last value into the removed slot and repairing its index.
tips: Update the swapped value’s position before removing the key.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: LFU frequency buckets
nodes.description: Evict by access frequency, breaking ties by recency.
nodes.approach: Keep an ordered bucket for each frequency and track the minimum active frequency. Access moves an item to the next frequency bucket.
tips: Updating an existing value counts as an access; new items start at frequency one.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 编程能力强化训练 / Part B

nodes.title: Lazy nested iterator
nodes.description: Flatten nested values without eagerly expanding the whole structure.
nodes.approach: Keep a stack of iterators. Advance the top iterator; push a child iterator for a nested list and pop exhausted iterators.
tips: hasNext implementations must not consume a value unless they cache it for next.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Circular buffer queue
nodes.description: Reuse a fixed capacity array for FIFO operations.
nodes.approach: Track a head index and count; the insertion position is (head+count) modulo capacity.
tips: Distinguish full and empty with a count rather than ambiguous equal pointers.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 四、队列 / §4.2 设计

nodes.title: Binary lifting ancestor queries
nodes.description: Answer large ancestor jumps repeatedly on a fixed tree.
nodes.approach: Precompute each node’s 2^b-th ancestor by composing two 2^(b−1) jumps. Decompose k into binary bits.
tips: Stop if an ancestor is absent or a requested bit exceeds the table.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 三、一般树 / §3.8 最近公共祖先（LCA）、倍增算法

nodes.title: Losing-state modular invariant
nodes.description: A small impartial game repeats after a fixed move range.
nodes.approach: Positions divisible by four are losing when players may remove one to three stones. From any other position move to a multiple of four.
tips: Explain the inductive losing-state argument, not just the modulo trick.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 四、博弈论

nodes.title: Multiplicative combinatorial counting
nodes.description: A path is an ordering of a fixed number of two move types.
nodes.approach: Choose which positions contain down moves among all moves. The answer is a binomial coefficient.
tips: Count move positions, not grid cells; there are m+n−2 moves.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

references.title: 二、组合数学 / §2.2 组合计数

nodes.title: Interactive monotone oracle
nodes.description: An API tells whether a guess is too low or too high.
nodes.approach: Binary search the hidden value using only the oracle response; preserve a closed interval of possible answers.
tips: The oracle compares your guess to the hidden number, so check its sign convention.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Reconstruct from traversal boundaries
nodes.description: A traversal identifies roots while another separates their subtrees.
nodes.approach: Preorder supplies the next root; an inorder index map divides the remaining range into left and right subtrees.
tips: Unique values are required for the index map to identify a single split.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

references.title: 二、二叉树 / §2.10 创建二叉树

nodes.title: Serialization with null markers
nodes.description: Preserve enough information to reconstruct both values and shape.
nodes.approach: Use preorder with an explicit marker for every absent child; decoding consumes exactly one token per recursive call.
tips: Values alone cannot distinguish different tree shapes.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

references.title: 二、二叉树 / §2.16 其他

nodes.title: Reverse a fixed-size group
nodes.description: Reverse complete chunks without changing leftover nodes.
nodes.approach: Find the kth node before mutating. Reverse links up to the following node, reconnect the group, and advance the group predecessor.
tips: Do not reverse a trailing group shorter than k.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 一、链表 / §1.4 反转链表

nodes.title: Midpoint split and half reversal
nodes.description: Compare symmetric linked-list values without an auxiliary array.
nodes.approach: Find the end of the first half using slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half, compare, then restore its links.
tips: Restoring the second half avoids surprising the caller with a mutated list.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

references.title: 一、链表 / §1.6 快慢指针

nodes.title: Partition by valid segments
nodes.description: Enumerate all ways to split a sequence into valid pieces.
nodes.approach: Choose the next ending boundary, recurse only when the chosen segment is a palindrome, then undo the segment.
tips: Each branch must advance the start index or recursion will not terminate.
nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

nodes.title: Minimum-remaining-values Sudoku search
nodes.description: Constraint satisfaction benefits from branching on the most restricted variable.
nodes.approach: Track used digits for each row, column, and box. At every step select the empty cell with fewest available candidates, then try and undo each candidate.
tips: An empty candidate set is an immediate contradiction.
nodes.why: Adds a new decision rule to your toolkit; study after the foundational patterns.

nodes.title: Resolve water from the lower boundary
nodes.description: Water at a position is limited by the smaller of two boundary maxima.

nodes.why: A reusable foundation: learn the invariant, then recognize it across different stories.

def solve(nums):

    left = 1
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        out[i] = left
        left *= x
    right = 1
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= right
        right *= nums[i]
    return out

solutions.approach: When the sum is too small, increase the left value; when too large, decrease the right value.
solutions.code:
def solve(numbers, target):
    left, right = 0, len(numbers)-1
    while left < right:
        total = numbers[left] + numbers[right]
        if total == target: return [left+1, right+1]
        if total < target: left += 1
        else: right -= 1

solutions.title: Fix one, solve two-sum
solutions.approach: Sort, fix the first value, then solve two-sum on the suffix; skip equal values at each decision boundary.
solutions.code:
def solve(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums); out = []
    for i in range(len(nums)-2):
        if i and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue
        left, right = i+1, len(nums)-1
        while left < right:
            s = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]
            if s < 0: left += 1
            elif s > 0: right -= 1
            else:
                out.append([nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]])
                left += 1; right -= 1
                while left < right and nums[left] == nums[left-1]: left += 1
                while left < right and nums[right] == nums[right+1]: right -= 1
    return out
solutions.space: O(n) for sorting copy, excluding output

solutions.approach: The shorter wall limits the area. Holding it while narrowing the interval cannot improve the answer, so move it.
solutions.code:
def solve(height):
    left, right, best = 0, len(height)-1, 0
    while left < right:
        best = max(best, (right-left)*min(height[left], height[right]))
        if height[left] <= height[right]: left += 1
        else: right -= 1
    return best

def solve(piles, h):

problems.title: Count Ways To Build Good Strings
problems.description: Build binary strings by appending either zero zeroes or one ones. Count distinct strings with lengths in [low,high], modulo 1,000,000,007.
problems.constraints: 1 ≤ low ≤ high; zero and one are positive block lengths.

solutions.title: Count by reachable length
solutions.approach: Let dp[length] count constructions of exactly that length. Add counts from length−zero and length−one, then sum the permitted interval.
solutions.code:
def solve(low, high, zero, one):
    mod = 1_000_000_007; dp = [0]*(high+1); dp[0] = 1
    for length in range(1, high+1):
        if length >= zero: dp[length] += dp[length-zero]
        if length >= one: dp[length] += dp[length-one]
        dp[length] %= mod
    return sum(dp[low:high+1]) % mod

def solve(nums):
    total = sum(nums)
    if total % 2: return False
    target = total//2; dp = [False]*(target+1); dp[0] = True
    for x in nums:
        for s in range(target, x-1, -1): dp[s] = dp[s] or dp[s-x]
    return dp[target]

solutions.code:
def solve(nums, target):
    total = sum(nums)
    if abs(target) > total or (total+target)%2: return 0
    goal = (total+target)//2; dp = [0]*(goal+1); dp[0] = 1
    for x in nums:
        for s in range(goal, x-1, -1): dp[s] += dp[s-x]
    return dp[goal]

def solve(points):

    def find(x):
        while x!=parent[x]: parent[x]=parent[parent[x]]; x=parent[x]
        return x
    edges=sorted((abs(a-c)+abs(b-d),i,j) for i,(a,b) in enumerate(points) for j,(c,d) in enumerate(points) if i<j)
    total=0; chosen=0

        if u==v: continue

def solve(s):
    n=len(s); sa=list(range(n)); rank=list(map(ord,s)); k=1
    while k<n:
        key=lambda i:(rank[i],rank[i+k] if i+k<n else -1)
        sa.sort(key=key); new=[0]*n
        for j in range(1,n): new[sa[j]]=new[sa[j-1]]+(key(sa[j-1])!=key(sa[j]))
        rank=new
        if rank[sa[-1]]==n-1: break
        k*=2
    position=[0]*n
    for i,start in enumerate(sa): position[start]=i
    length=best=start=0
    for i in range(n):
        r=position[i]
        if r==0: length=0; continue
        j=sa[r-1]
        while i+length<n and j+length<n and s[i+length]==s[j+length]: length+=1
        if length>best: best,start=length,i
        length=max(0,length-1)
    return s[start:start+best]

def solve(n,a,b,c):
    from math import lcm
    ab,ac,bc,abc=lcm(a,b),lcm(a,c),lcm(b,c),lcm(a,b,c)
    left,right=1,n*min(a,b,c)
    while left<right:
        x=(left+right)//2
        count=x//a+x//b+x//c-x//ab-x//ac-x//bc+x//abc
        if count>=n: right=x
        else: left=x+1
    return left

solutions.code:
def solve(head):
    if head is None: return True
    slow=fast=head
    while fast.next and fast.next.next: slow=slow.next; fast=fast.next.next
    def reverse(node):
        previous=None
        while node: nxt=node.next; node.next=previous; previous=node; node=nxt
        return previous
    second=reverse(slow.next); a,b=head,second; valid=True
    while b:
        if a.val!=b.val: valid=False
        a=a.next; b=b.next
    slow.next=reverse(second)
    return valid

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def swapPairs(self, head: ListNode) -> ListNode:
    def getLength(head: ListNode) -> int:
      length = 0
      while head:
        length += 1
        head = head.next
      return length

    length = getLength(head)
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    prev = dummy
    curr = head

    for _ in range(length // 2):
      next = curr.next
      curr.next = next.next
      next.next = prev.next
      prev.next = next
      prev = curr
      curr = curr.next

    return dummy.next

class Solution:
  def insert(self, intervals: list[list[int]],
             newInterval: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    n = len(intervals)
    ans = []
    i = 0

    while i < n and intervals[i][1] < newInterval[0]:
      ans.append(intervals[i])
      i += 1

    # Merge overlapping intervals.
    while i < n and intervals[i][0] <= newInterval[1]:
      newInterval[0] = min(newInterval[0], intervals[i][0])
      newInterval[1] = max(newInterval[1], intervals[i][1])
      i += 1

    ans.append(newInterval)

    while i < n:
      ans.append(intervals[i])
      i += 1

    return ans

class Solution:
  def getPermutation(self, n: int, k: int) -> str:
    ans = ''
    nums = [i + 1 for i in range(n)]
    fact = [1] * (n + 1)  # fact[i] := i!

    for i in range(2, n + 1):
      fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i

    k -= 1  # 0-indexed

    for i in reversed(range(n)):
      j = k // fact[i]
      k %= fact[i]
      ans += str(nums[j])
      nums.pop(j)

    return ans

class Solution:
  def fullJustify(self, words: list[str], maxWidth: int) -> list[str]:
    ans = []
    row = []
    rowLetters = 0

    for word in words:
      # If we place the word in this row, it will exceed the maximum width.
      # Therefore, we cannot put the word in this row and have to pad spaces
      # for each word in this row.
      if rowLetters + len(word) + len(row) > maxWidth:
        for i in range(maxWidth - rowLetters):
          row[i % (len(row) - 1 or 1)] += ' '
        ans.append(''.join(row))
        row = []
        rowLetters = 0
      row.append(word)
      rowLetters += len(word)

    return ans + [' '.join(row).ljust(maxWidth)]

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def partition(self, head: ListNode, x: int) -> ListNode:
    beforeHead = ListNode(0)
    afterHead = ListNode(0)
    before = beforeHead
    after = afterHead

    while head:
      if head.val < x:
        before.next = head
        before = head
      else:
        after.next = head
        after = head
      head = head.next

    after.next = None
    before.next = afterHead.next

    return beforeHead.next

class Solution:
  def sortedListToBST(self, head: ListNode | None) -> TreeNode | None:
    def helper(l: int, r: int) -> TreeNode | None:
      nonlocal head
      if l > r:
        return None

      m = (l + r) // 2

      # Simulate inorder traversal: recursively form the left half.
      left = helper(l, m - 1)

      # Once the left half is traversed, process the current node.
      root = TreeNode(head.val)
      root.left = left

      # Maintain the invariance.
      head = head.next

      # Simulate inorder traversal: recursively form the right half.
      root.right = helper(m + 1, r)
      return root

    return helper(0, self._getLength(head) - 1)

  def _getLength(self, head: ListNode | None) -> int:
    length = 0
    curr = head
    while curr:
      length += 1
      curr = curr.next
    return length

  def flatten(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> None:
    if not root:

    sellTwo = 0
    holdTwo = -math.inf
    sellOne = 0

class Solution:
  def reorderList(self, head: ListNode) -> None:
    def findMid(head: ListNode):
      prev = None
      slow = head
      fast = head

      while fast and fast.next:
        prev = slow
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
      prev.next = None

      return slow

    def reverse(head: ListNode) -> ListNode:
      prev = None
      curr = head

      while curr:
        next = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = next

      return prev

    def merge(l1: ListNode, l2: ListNode) -> None:
      while l2:
        next = l1.next
        l1.next = l2
        l1 = l2
        l2 = next

    if not head or not head.next:
      return

    mid = findMid(head)
    reversed = reverse(mid)
    merge(head, reversed)

class Solution:
  def insertionSortList(self, head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None:
    dummy = ListNode(0)
    prev = dummy  # the last and thus largest of the sorted list

    while head:  # the current inserting node
      next = head.next  # Cache the next inserting node.
      if prev.val >= head.val:
        prev = dummy  # Move `prev` to the front.
      while prev.next and prev.next.val < head.val:
        prev = prev.next
      head.next = prev.next
      prev.next = head
      head = next  # Update the current inserting node.

    return dummy.next

class Solution:
  def sortList(self, head: ListNode) -> ListNode:
    def split(head: ListNode, k: int) -> ListNode:
      while k > 1 and head:
        head = head.next
        k -= 1
      rest = head.next if head else None
      if head:
        head.next = None
      return rest

    def merge(l1: ListNode, l2: ListNode) -> tuple:
      dummy = ListNode(0)
      tail = dummy

      while l1 and l2:
        if l1.val > l2.val:
          l1, l2 = l2, l1
        tail.next = l1
        l1 = l1.next
        tail = tail.next
      tail.next = l1 if l1 else l2
      while tail.next:
        tail = tail.next

      return dummy.next, tail

    length = 0
    curr = head
    while curr:
      length += 1
      curr = curr.next

    dummy = ListNode(0, head)

    k = 1
    while k < length:
      curr = dummy.next
      tail = dummy
      while curr:
        l = curr
        r = split(l, k)
        curr = split(r, k)
        mergedHead, mergedTail = merge(l, r)
        tail.next = mergedHead
        tail = mergedTail
      k *= 2

    return dummy.next

class Solution:
  def upsideDownBinaryTree(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> TreeNode | None:
    prevRoot = None
    prevRightChild = None

    while root:
      nextRoot = root.left  # Cache the next root.
      root.left = prevRightChild
      prevRightChild = root.right
      root.right = prevRoot
      prevRoot = root  # Record the previous root.
      root = nextRoot  # Update the root.

    return prevRoot

    i4 = 0  # buf4's index
    n4 = 0  # buf4's size
    i = 0  # buf's index

    while i < n:

      buf[i] = buf4[i4]
      i += 1
      i4 += 1

    return i

class Solution:
  def findOrder(
      self,
      numCourses: int,
      prerequisites: list[list[int]],
  ) -> list[int]:
    ans = []
    graph = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)]
    inDegrees = [0] * numCourses
    q = collections.deque()

    # Build the graph.
    for v, u in prerequisites:
      graph[u].append(v)
      inDegrees[v] += 1

    # Perform topological sorting.
    q = collections.deque([i for i, d in enumerate(inDegrees) if d == 0])

    while q:
      u = q.popleft()
      ans.append(u)
      for v in graph[u]:
        inDegrees[v] -= 1
        if inDegrees[v] == 0:
          q.append(v)

    return ans if len(ans) == numCourses else []

class Solution:
  def computeArea(self,
                  A: int, B: int, C: int, D: int,
                  E: int, F: int, G: int, H: int) -> int:
    x = min(C, G) - max(A, E) if max(A, E) < min(C, G) else 0
    y = min(D, H) - max(B, F) if max(B, F) < min(D, H) else 0
    return (C - A) * (D - B) + (G - E) * (H - F) - x * y

class Solution:
  def minCostII(self, costs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    prevIndex = -1  # the previous minimum index
    prevMin1 = 0  # the minimum cost so far
    prevMin2 = 0  # the second minimum cost so far

    for cost in costs:  # O(n)
      # the painted index that will achieve the minimum cost after painting the
      # current house
      index = -1
      # the minimum cost after painting the current house
      min1 = math.inf
      # the second minimum cost after painting the current house
      min2 = math.inf
      for i, cst in enumerate(cost):   # O(k)
        theCost = cst + (prevMin2 if i == prevIndex else prevMin1)
        if theCost < min1:
          index = i
          min2 = min1
          min1 = theCost
        elif theCost < min2:  # min1 <= theCost < min2
          min2 = theCost

      prevIndex = index
      prevMin1 = min1
      prevMin2 = min2

    return prevMin1

class Solution:
  def minTotalDistance(self, grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    m = len(grid)
    n = len(grid[0])
    # i indices s.t. grid[i][j] == 1
    I = [i for i in range(m) for j in range(n) if grid[i][j]]
    # j indices s.t. grid[i][j] == 1
    J = [j for j in range(n) for i in range(m) if grid[i][j]]

    def minTotalDistance(grid: list[int]) -> int:
      summ = 0
      i = 0
      j = len(grid) - 1
      while i < j:
        summ += grid[j] - grid[i]
        i += 1
        j -= 1
      return summ

    # sum(i - median(I)) + sum(j - median(J))
    return minTotalDistance(I) + minTotalDistance(J)

class Solution:
  def minArea(self, image: list[list[str]], x: int, y: int) -> int:
    DIRS = ((0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0))
    m = len(image)
    n = len(image[0])
    topLeft = [x, y]
    bottomRight = [x, y]
    q = collections.deque([(x, y)])
    image[x][y] = '2'  # Mark as visited.

    while q:
      i, j = q.popleft()
      for dx, dy in DIRS:
        r = i + dx
        c = j + dy
        if r < 0 or r == m or c < 0 or c == n:
          continue
        if image[r][c] != '1':
          continue
        topLeft[0] = min(topLeft[0], r)
        topLeft[1] = min(topLeft[1], c)
        bottomRight[0] = max(bottomRight[0], r)
        bottomRight[1] = max(bottomRight[1], c)
        q.append((r, c))
        image[r][c] = '2'

    width = bottomRight[1] - topLeft[1] + 1
    height = bottomRight[0] - topLeft[0] + 1
    return width * height

class Solution:
  def generateAbbreviations(self, word: str) -> list[str]:
    ans = []

    def getCountString(count: int) -> str:
      return str(count) if count > 0 else ''

    def dfs(i: int, count: int, path: list[str]) -> None:
      if i == len(word):
        ans.append(''.join(path) + getCountString(count))
        return

      # Abbreviate the word[i].
      dfs(i + 1, count + 1, path)
      # Keep the word[i], so consume the count as a string.
      path.append(getCountString(count) + word[i])
      # Reset the count to 0.
      dfs(i + 1, 0, path)
      path.pop()

    dfs(0, 0, [])
    return ans

class Solution:
  def countRangeSum(self, nums: list[int], lower: int, upper: int) -> int:
    n = len(nums)
    self.ans = 0
    prefix = list(itertools.accumulate(nums, initial=0))

    self._mergeSort(prefix, 0, n, lower, upper)
    return self.ans

  def _mergeSort(
      self,
      prefix: list[int],
      l: int,
      r: int,
      lower: int,
      upper: int,
  ) -> None:
    if l >= r:
      return

    m = (l + r) // 2
    self._mergeSort(prefix, l, m, lower, upper)
    self._mergeSort(prefix, m + 1, r, lower, upper)
    self._merge(prefix, l, m, r, lower, upper)

  def _merge(
      self,
      prefix: list[int],
      l: int,
      m: int,
      r: int,
      lower: int,
      upper: int,
  ) -> None:
    lo = m + 1  # the first index s.t. prefix[lo] - prefix[i] >= lower
    hi = m + 1  # the first index s.t. prefix[hi] - prefix[i] > upper

    # For each index i in range [l, m], add hi - lo to `ans`.
    for i in range(l, m + 1):
      while lo <= r and prefix[lo] - prefix[i] < lower:
        lo += 1
      while hi <= r and prefix[hi] - prefix[i] <= upper:
        hi += 1
      self.ans += hi - lo

    sorted = [0] * (r - l + 1)
    k = 0  # sorted's index
    i = l  # left's index
    j = m + 1  # right's index

    while i <= m and j <= r:
      if prefix[i] < prefix[j]:
        sorted[k] = prefix[i]
        k += 1
        i += 1
      else:
        sorted[k] = prefix[j]
        k += 1
        j += 1

    # Put the possible remaining left part into the sorted array.
    while i <= m:
      sorted[k] = prefix[i]
      k += 1
      i += 1

    # Put the possible remaining right part into the sorted array.
    while j <= r:
      sorted[k] = prefix[j]
      k += 1
      j += 1

    prefix[l:l + len(sorted)] = sorted

class Solution:
  def oddEvenList(self, head: ListNode) -> ListNode:
    oddHead = ListNode(0)
    evenHead = ListNode(0)
    odd = oddHead
    even = evenHead
    isOdd = True

    while head:
      if isOdd:
        odd.next = head
        odd = head
      else:
        even.next = head
        even = head
      head = head.next
      isOdd = not isOdd

    even.next = None
    odd.next = evenHead.next
    return oddHead.next

class Solution:
  def isPowerOfFour(self, n: int) -> bool:
    # Why (4^n - 1) % 3 == 0?
    # (4^n - 1) = (2^n - 1)(2^n + 1) and 2^n - 1, 2^n, 2^n + 1 are
    # three consecutive numbers; among one of them, there must be a multiple
    # of 3, and that can't be 2^n, so it must be either 2^n - 1 or 2^n + 1.
    # Therefore, 4^n - 1 is a multiple of 3.
    return n > 0 and n.bit_count() == 1 and (n - 1) % 3 == 0

class Solution:
  def integerBreak(self, n: int) -> int:
    # If an optimal product contains a factor f >= 4, then we can replace it
    # with 2 and f - 2 without losing optimality. As 2(f - 2) = 2f - 4 >= f,
    # we never need a factor >= 4, meaning we only need factors 1, 2, and 3
    # (and 1 is wasteful).
    # Also, 3 * 3 is better than 2 * 2 * 2, so we never use 2 more than twice.
    if n == 2:  # 1 * 1
      return 1
    if n == 3:  # 1 * 2
      return 2

    ans = 1

    while n > 4:
      n -= 3
      ans *= 3
    ans *= n

    return ans

solutions.code:
class SnakeGame:
  def __init__(self, width: int, height: int, food: list[list[int]]):
    """
    Initialize your data structure here.
    @param width - screen width
    @param height - screen height
    @param food - A list of food positions
    E.g food = [[1,1], [1,0]] means the first food is positioned at [1,1], the second is at [1,0].
    """
    self.width = width
    self.height = height
    self.food = food
    self.score = 0
    self.k = 0  # food's index
    self.lookup = set([self.getId(0, 0)])
    self.body = collections.deque([self.getId(0, 0)])  # snake's body

  def move(self, direction: str) -> int:
    """
    Moves the snake.
    @param direction - 'U' = Up, 'L' = Left, 'R' = Right, 'D' = Down
    @return The game's score after the move. Return -1 if game over.
    Game over when snake crosses the screen boundary or bites its body.
    """
    # the old head's position
    i = self.body[0] // self.width
    j = self.body[0] % self.width

    # Update the head's position and check if it's out-of-bounds.
    if direction == "U":
      i -= 1
      if i < 0:
        return -1
    if direction == "L":
      j -= 1
      if j < 0:
        return -1
    if direction == "R":
      j += 1
      if j == self.width:
        return -1
    if direction == "D":
      i += 1
      if i == self.height:
        return -1

    newHead = self.getId(i, j)

    # 1. Eat food and increase the size by 1.
    if self.k < len(self.food) and i == self.food[self.k][0] and j == self.food[self.k][1]:
      self.lookup.add(newHead)
      self.body.appendleft(newHead)
      self.k += 1
      self.score += 1
      return self.score

    # 2. new head != old tail and eat body!
    if newHead != self.body[-1] and newHead in self.lookup:
      return -1

    # 3. normal case
    # Remove the old tail first, then add new head because new head may be in
    # old tail's position.
    self.lookup.remove(self.body[-1])
    self.lookup.add(newHead)
    self.body.pop()
    self.body.appendleft(newHead)

    return self.score

  def getId(self, i: int, j: int) -> int:
    return i * self.width + j

class Solution:
  def isReflected(self, points: list[list[int]]) -> bool:
    minX = math.inf
    maxX = -math.inf
    seen = set()

    for x, y in points:
      minX = min(minX, x)
      maxX = max(maxX, x)
      seen.add((x, y))

    summ = minX + maxX
    # (leftX + rightX) / 2 = (minX + maxX) / 2
    #  leftX = minX + maxX - rightX
    # rightX = minX + maxX - leftX

    return all((summ - x, y) in seen for x, y in points)

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def sortTransformedArray(
      self,
      nums: list[int],
      a: int,
      b: int,
      c: int,
  ) -> list[int]:
    n = len(nums)
    upward = a > 0
    ans = [0] * n

    # The concavity of f only depends on a's sign.
    def f(x: int, a: int, b: int, c: int) -> int:
      return (a * x + b) * x + c

    quad = [f(num, a, b, c) for num in nums]

    i = n - 1 if upward else 0
    l = 0
    r = n - 1
    while l <= r:
      if upward:  # is the maximum in the both ends
        if quad[l] > quad[r]:
          ans[i] = quad[l]
          l += 1
        else:
          ans[i] = quad[r]
          r -= 1
        i -= 1
      else:  # is the minimum in the both ends
        if quad[l] < quad[r]:
          ans[i] = quad[l]
          l += 1
        else:
          ans[i] = quad[r]
          r -= 1
        i += 1

    return ans

class Solution:
  def findLeaves(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[list[int]]:
    ans = []

    def depth(root: TreeNode | None) -> int:
      """Returns the depth of the root (0-indexed)."""
      if not root:
        return -1

      l = depth(root.left)
      r = depth(root.right)
      h = 1 + max(l, r)

      if len(ans) == h:  # Meet a leaf
        ans.append([])

      ans[h].append(root.val)
      return h

    depth(root)
    return ans

class Solution:
  def lengthLongestPath(self, input: str) -> int:
    ans = 0
    stack = [(-1, 0)]  # placeholder

    for token in input.split('\n'):
      depth = token.count('\t')
      token = token.replace('\t', '')
      while depth <= stack[-1][0]:
        stack.pop()
      if '.' in token:  # `token` is file.
        ans = max(ans, stack[-1][1] + len(token))
      else:  # directory + '/'
        stack.append((depth, stack[-1][1] + len(token) + 1))

    return ans

class Solution:
  def isRectangleCover(self, rectangles: list[list[int]]) -> bool:
    area = 0
    x1 = math.inf
    y1 = math.inf
    x2 = -math.inf
    y2 = -math.inf
    corners: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()

    for x, y, a, b in rectangles:
      area += (a - x) * (b - y)
      x1 = min(x1, x)
      y1 = min(y1, y)
      x2 = max(x2, a)
      y2 = max(y2, b)

      # the four points of the current rectangle
      for point in [(x, y), (x, b), (a, y), (a, b)]:
        if point in corners:
          corners.remove(point)
        else:
          corners.add(point)

    if len(corners) != 4:
      return False
    if ((x1, y1) not in corners or
        (x1, y2) not in corners or
        (x2, y1) not in corners or
            (x2, y2) not in corners):
      return False
    return area == (x2 - x1) * (y2 - y1)

class Solution:
  def integerReplacement(self, n: int) -> int:
    ans = 0

    while n > 1:
      if n % 2 == 0:  # `n` ends in 0.
        n >>= 1
      elif n == 3 or (n >> 1 & 1) == 0:  # `n` = 3 or ends in 0b01.
        n -= 1
      else:  # `n` ends in 0b11.
        n += 1
      ans += 1

    return ans

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def trapRainWater(self, heightMap: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    DIRS = ((0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0))
    m = len(heightMap)
    n = len(heightMap[0])
    ans = 0
    minHeap = []
    seen = set()

    for i in range(m):
      heapq.heappush(minHeap, (heightMap[i][0], i, 0))
      heapq.heappush(minHeap, (heightMap[i][n - 1], i, n - 1))
      seen.add((i, 0))
      seen.add((i, n - 1))

    for j in range(1, n - 1):
      heapq.heappush(minHeap, (heightMap[0][j], 0, j))
      heapq.heappush(minHeap, (heightMap[m - 1][j], m - 1, j))
      seen.add((0, j))
      seen.add((m - 1, j))

    while minHeap:
      h, i, j = heapq.heappop(minHeap)
      for dx, dy in DIRS:
        x = i + dx
        y = j + dy
        if x < 0 or x == m or y < 0 or y == n:
          continue
        if (x, y) in seen:
          continue
        if heightMap[x][y] < h:
          ans += h - heightMap[x][y]
          # Fill water in grid[x][y].
          heapq.heappush(minHeap, (h, x, y))
        else:
          heapq.heappush(minHeap, (heightMap[x][y], x, y))
        seen.add((x, y))

    return ans

solutions.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Record:
  count: int
  nextIndex: int


class Solution:
  def getMaxRepetitions(self, s1: str, n1: int, s2: str, n2: int) -> int:
    # records[i].count := the number of times that s2 starting from index i has
    # been fully matched with s1
    # records[i].nextIndex := the next index in s2 to be matched after
    # completing a full match starting from index i
    records = []

    for nextIndex in range(len(s2)):
      count = 0
      for c in s1:
        if s2[nextIndex] == c:
          nextIndex += 1
          if nextIndex == len(s2):  # There's a match.
            count += 1
            nextIndex = 0
      records.append(Record(count, nextIndex))

    matches = 0  # the number of matches between `s1` x n1 and `s2`
    i = 0  # the index in `s2` to start matching

    for _ in range(n1):
      matches += records[i].count
      i = records[i].nextIndex

    return matches // n2

class Solution:
  def __init__(self, radius: float, x_center: float, y_center: float):
    self.radius = radius
    self.x_center = x_center
    self.y_center = y_center

  def randPoint(self) -> list[float]:
    length = math.sqrt(random.uniform(0, 1)) * self.radius
    degree = random.uniform(0, 1) * 2 * math.pi
    x = self.x_center + length * math.cos(degree)
    y = self.y_center + length * math.sin(degree)
    return [x, y]

class Solution:
  def boundaryOfBinaryTree(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[int]:
    if not root:
      return []

    ans = [root.val]

    def dfs(root: TreeNode | None, lb: bool, rb: bool):
      """
      1. root.left is left boundary if root is left boundary.
         root.right if left boundary if root.left is None.
      2. Same applys for right boundary.
      3. If root is left boundary, add it before 2 children - preorder.
         If root is right boundary, add it after 2 children - postorder.
      4. A leaf that is neighter left/right boundary belongs to the bottom.
      """
      if not root:
        return
      if lb:
        ans.append(root.val)
      if not lb and not rb and not root.left and not root.right:
        ans.append(root.val)

      dfs(root.left, lb, rb and not root.right)
      dfs(root.right, lb and not root.left, rb)
      if rb:
        ans.append(root.val)

    dfs(root.left, True, False)
    dfs(root.right, False, True)
    return ans

class Solution:
  def checkRecord(self, n: int) -> int:
    MOD = 1_000_000_007
    # dp[i][j] := the length so far with i A's and the last letters are j L's
    dp = [[0] * 3 for _ in range(2)]
    dp[0][0] = 1

    for _ in range(n):
      prev = [A[:] for A in dp]

      # Append a P.
      dp[0][0] = (prev[0][0] + prev[0][1] + prev[0][2]) % MOD

      # Append an L.
      dp[0][1] = prev[0][0]

      # Append an L.
      dp[0][2] = prev[0][1]

      # Append an A or append a P.
      dp[1][0] = (prev[0][0] + prev[0][1] + prev[0][2] +
                  prev[1][0] + prev[1][1] + prev[1][2]) % MOD

      # Append an L.
      dp[1][1] = prev[1][0]

      # Append an L.
      dp[1][2] = prev[1][1]

    return (sum(dp[0]) + sum(dp[1])) % MOD

class Solution:
  def longestLine(self, mat: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    m = len(mat)
    n = len(mat[0])
    ans = 0
    # dp[i][j][0] := horizontal
    # dp[i][j][1] := vertical
    # dp[i][j][2] := diagonal
    # dp[i][j][3] := anti-diagonal
    dp = [[[0] * 4 for j in range(n)] for _ in range(m)]

    for i in range(m):
      for j in range(n):
        if mat[i][j] == 1:
          dp[i][j][0] = dp[i][j - 1][0] + 1 if j > 0 else 1
          dp[i][j][1] = dp[i - 1][j][1] + 1 if i > 0 else 1
          dp[i][j][2] = dp[i - 1][j - 1][2] + 1 if i > 0 and j > 0 else 1
          dp[i][j][3] = dp[i - 1][j + 1][3] + 1 if i > 0 and j < n - 1 else 1
          ans = max(ans, max(dp[i][j]))

    return ans

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def findDuplicate(self, paths: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
    contentToPathFiles = collections.defaultdict(list)

    for path in paths:
      words = path.split(' ')
      rootPath = words[0]  # "root/d1/d2/.../dm"
      for fileAndContent in words[1:]:  # "fn.txt(fn_content)"
        l = fileAndContent.find('(')
        r = fileAndContent.find(')')
        # "fn.txt"
        file = fileAndContent[:l]
        # "fn_content"
        content = fileAndContent[l + 1:r]
        # "root/d1/d2/.../dm/fn.txt"
        filePath = rootPath + '/' + file
        contentToPathFiles[content].append(filePath)

    return [filePath for filePath in contentToPathFiles.values() if len(filePath) > 1]

class Solution:
  def mergeTrees(
      self,
      root1: TreeNode | None,
      root2: TreeNode | None,
  ) -> TreeNode | None:
    if not root1 and not root2:
      return None
    val = (root1.val if root1 else 0) + (root2.val if root2 else 0)
    root = TreeNode(val)
    root.left = self.mergeTrees(root1.left if root1 else None,
                                root2.left if root2 else None)
    root.right = self.mergeTrees(root1.right if root1 else None,
                                 root2.right if root2 else None)
    return root

class Solution:
  def leastInterval(self, tasks: list[str], n: int) -> int:
    count = collections.Counter(tasks)
    maxFreq = max(count.values())
    # Put the most frequent task in the slot first.
    maxFreqTaskOccupy = (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1)
    # Get the number of tasks with same frequency as maxFreq, we'll append them after the
    # `maxFreqTaskOccupy`.
    nMaxFreq = sum(value == maxFreq for value in count.values())
    # max(
    #   the most frequent task is frequent enough to force some idle slots,
    #   the most frequent task is not frequent enough to force idle slots
    # )
    return max(maxFreqTaskOccupy + nMaxFreq, len(tasks))

class Solution:
  def calPoints(self, operations: list[str]) -> int:
    scores = []

    for operation in operations:
      match operation:
        case '+':
          scores.append(scores[-1] + scores[-2])
        case 'D':
          scores.append(scores[-1] * 2)
        case 'C':
          scores.pop()
        case default:
          scores.append(int(operation))

    return sum(scores)

class Solution:
  def kEmptySlots(self, bulbs: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    n = len(bulbs)
    ans = math.inf
    # day[i] := the day when bulbs[i] is turned on
    day = [0] * n

    for i, bulb in enumerate(bulbs):
      day[bulb - 1] = i + 1

    # Find a subarray of day[l..r], where its length is k + 2.
    # For each l < i < r, day[i] > max(day[l], day[r]).
    l = 0
    r = l + k + 1
    i = 1
    while r < n:
      if i == r:
        ans = min(ans, max(day[l], day[r]))
        l = i
        r = i + k + 1
      elif day[i] < max(day[l], day[r]):
        l = i
        r = i + k + 1
      i += 1

    return -1 if ans == math.inf else ans

class Solution:
  def maxSumOfThreeSubarrays(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(nums) - k + 1
    # sums[i] := sum(nums[i..i + k))
    sums = [0] * n
    # l[i] := the index in [0..i] that has the maximum sums[i]
    l = [0] * n
    # r[i] := the index in [i..n) that has the maximum sums[i]
    r = [0] * n

    summ = 0
    for i, num in enumerate(nums):
      summ += num
      if i >= k:
        summ -= nums[i - k]
      if i >= k - 1:
        sums[i - k + 1] = summ

    maxIndex = 0
    for i in range(n):
      if sums[i] > sums[maxIndex]:
        maxIndex = i
      l[i] = maxIndex

    maxIndex = n - 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
      if sums[i] >= sums[maxIndex]:
        maxIndex = i
      r[i] = maxIndex

    ans = [-1, -1, -1]

    for i in range(k, n - k):
      if (ans[0] == -1 or
          sums[ans[0]] + sums[ans[1]] + sums[ans[2]] <
              sums[l[i - k]] + sums[i] + sums[r[i + k]]):
        ans[0] = l[i - k]
        ans[1] = i
        ans[2] = r[i + k]

    return ans

class Solution:
  def hasAlternatingBits(self, n: int) -> bool:
    #            n = 0b010101
    #       n >> 2 = 0b000101
    # n ^ (n >> 2) = 0b010000 = a
    #        a - 1 = 0b001111
    #  a & (a - 1) = 0
    a = n ^ (n >> 2)
    return (a & (a - 1)) == 0

class Solution:
  def splitListToParts(self, root: ListNode, k: int) -> list[ListNode]:
    ans = [[] for _ in range(k)]
    length = 0
    curr = root
    while curr:
      length += 1
      curr = curr.next
    subLength = length // k
    remainder = length % k

    prev = None
    head = root

    for i in range(k):
      ans[i] = head
      for j in range(subLength + (1 if remainder > 0 else 0)):
        prev = head
        head = head.next
      if prev:
        prev.next = None
      remainder -= 1

    return ans

class Solution:
  def floodFill(self, image: list[list[int]],
                sr: int, sc: int, newColor: int) -> list[list[int]]:
    startColor = image[sr][sc]
    seen = set()

    def dfs(i: int, j: int) -> None:
      if i < 0 or i == len(image) or j < 0 or j == len(image[0]):
        return
      if image[i][j] != startColor or (i, j) in seen:
        return

      image[i][j] = newColor
      seen.add((i, j))

      dfs(i + 1, j)
      dfs(i - 1, j)
      dfs(i, j + 1)
      dfs(i, j - 1)

    dfs(sr, sc)
    return image

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def reorganizeString(self, s: str) -> str:
    count = collections.Counter(s)
    if max(count.values()) > (len(s) + 1) // 2:
      return ''

    ans = []
    maxHeap = [(-freq, c) for c, freq in count.items()]
    heapq.heapify(maxHeap)
    prevFreq = 0
    prevChar = '@'

    while maxHeap:
      # Get the letter with the maximum frequency.
      freq, c = heapq.heappop(maxHeap)
      ans.append(c)
      # Add the previous letter back s.t. any two adjacent characters are not
      # the same.
      if prevFreq < 0:
        heapq.heappush(maxHeap, (prevFreq, prevChar))
      prevFreq = freq + 1
      prevChar = c

    return ''.join(ans)

class Solution:
  def numSubarrayBoundedMax(
      self,
      nums: list[int],
      left: int,
      right: int,
  ) -> int:

class Solution:
  def maxProfitAssignment(
      self,
      difficulty: list[int],
      profit: list[int],
      worker: list[int],
  ) -> int:
    ans = 0
    jobs = sorted(zip(difficulty, profit))
    worker.sort(reverse=1)

    i = 0
    maxProfit = 0

    for w in sorted(worker):
      while i < len(jobs) and w >= jobs[i][0]:
        maxProfit = max(maxProfit, jobs[i][1])
        i += 1
      ans += maxProfit

    return ans

class Solution:
  def uniqueLetterString(self, s: str) -> int:
    ans = 0
    # the number of unique letters in all the substrings ending in the index so
    # far
    dp = 0
    lastCount = {}
    lastSeen = {}

    for i, c in enumerate(s):
      newCount = i - lastSeen.get(c, -1)
      # Substract the duplicates.
      dp -= lastCount.get(c, 0)
      # Add count of s[lastSeen[c] + 1..i], s[lastSeen[c] + 2..i], ..., s[i].
      dp += newCount
      lastCount[c] = newCount
      lastSeen[c] = i
      ans += dp

    return ans

class Solution:
  def new21Game(self, n: int, k: int, maxPts: int) -> float:
    # When the game ends, the point is in [k..k - 1 maxPts].
    #   P = 1, if n >= k - 1 + maxPts
    #   P = 0, if n < k (note that the constraints already have k <= n)
    if k == 0 or n >= k - 1 + maxPts:
      return 1.0

    ans = 0.0
    dp = [1.0] + [0] * n  # dp[i] := the probability to have i points
    windowSum = dp[0]  # P(i - 1) + P(i - 2) + ... + P(i - maxPts)

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
      # The probability to get i points is
      # P(i) = [P(i - 1) + P(i - 2) + ... + P(i - maxPts)] / maxPts
      dp[i] = windowSum / maxPts
      if i < k:
        windowSum += dp[i]
      else:  # The game ends.
        ans += dp[i]
      if i - maxPts >= 0:
        windowSum -= dp[i - maxPts]

    return ans

# """
# This is Master's API interface.
# You should not implement it, or speculate about its implementation
# """
# Class Master:
#   def guess(self, word: str) -> int:

class Solution:
  def findSecretWord(self, words: list[str], master: 'Master') -> None:
    for _ in range(10):
      guessedWord = words[random.randint(0, len(words) - 1)]
      matches = master.guess(guessedWord)
      if matches == 6:
        break
      words = [
          word for word in words
          if sum(c1 == c2 for c1, c2 in zip(guessedWord, word)) == matches]

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def minRefuelStops(
      self,
      target: int,
      startFuel: int,
      stations: list[list[int]],
  ) -> int:
    ans = 0
    i = 0  # station's index
    curr = startFuel
    maxHeap = []

    while curr < target:
      # Add all the reachable stops to maxHeap
      while i < len(stations) and stations[i][0] <= curr:
        heapq.heappush(maxHeap, -stations[i][1])
        i += 1
      if not maxHeap:  # Can't be refueled.
        return -1
      curr -= heapq.heappop(maxHeap)  # Pop out the largest gas.
      ans += 1  # Then, refuel once.

    return ans

solutions.code:
class Solution:
  def sumSubseqWidths(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
    MOD = 1_000_000_007
    n = len(nums)
    ans = 0
    exp = 1

    nums.sort()

    for i in range(n):
      ans += (nums[i] - nums[n - 1 - i]) * exp
      ans %= MOD
      exp = exp * 2 % MOD

    return ans

class Solution:
  def superpalindromesInRange(self, left: str, right: str) -> int:
    def nextPalindrome(num: int) -> int:
      s = str(num)
      n = len(s)

      half = s[0:(n + 1) // 2]
      reversedHalf = half[:n // 2][::-1]
      candidate = int(half + reversedHalf)
      if candidate >= num:
        return candidate

      half = str(int(half) + 1)
      reversedHalf = half[:n // 2][::-1]
      return int(half + reversedHalf)

    def isPalindrome(num: int) -> bool:
      s = str(num)
      l = 0
      r = len(s) - 1

      while l < r:
        if s[l] != s[r]:
          return False
        l += 1
        r -= 1

      return True

    ans = 0
    l = int(left)
    r = int(right)
    i = math.isqrt(l)

    while i * i <= r:
      palindrome = nextPalindrome(i)
      squared = palindrome**2
      if squared <= r and isPalindrome(squared):
        ans += 1
      i = palindrome + 1

    return ans

class Solution:
  def smallestRangeII(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    nums.sort()

    ans = nums[-1] - nums[0]
    left = nums[0] + k
    right = nums[-1] - k

    for a, b in itertools.pairwise(nums):
      mn = min(left, b - k)
      mx = max(right, a + k)
      ans = min(ans, mx - mn)

    return ans

from enum import IntEnum


class State(IntEnum):
  DRAW = 0
  MOUSE_WIN = 1
  CAT_WIN = 2


class Solution:
  def catMouseGame(self, graph: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    n = len(graph)
    # result of (cat, mouse, move)
    # move := 0 (mouse) // 1 (cat)
    states = [[[0] * 2 for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    outDegree = [[[0] * 2 for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    q = collections.deque()  # (cat, mouse, move, state)

    for cat in range(n):
      for mouse in range(n):
        outDegree[cat][mouse][0] = len(graph[mouse])
        outDegree[cat][mouse][1] = len(graph[cat]) - graph[cat].count(0)

    # Start from the states s.t. the winner can be determined.
    for cat in range(1, n):
      for move in range(2):
        # Mouse is in the hole.
        states[cat][0][move] = int(State.MOUSE_WIN)
        q.append((cat, 0, move, int(State.MOUSE_WIN)))
        # Cat catches mouse.
        states[cat][cat][move] = int(State.CAT_WIN)
        q.append((cat, cat, move, int(State.CAT_WIN)))

    while q:
      cat, mouse, move, state = q.popleft()
      if cat == 2 and mouse == 1 and move == 0:
        return state
      prevMove = move ^ 1
      for prev in graph[cat if prevMove else mouse]:
        prevCat = prev if prevMove else cat
        if prevCat == 0:  # invalid
          continue
        prevMouse = mouse if prevMove else prev
        # The state has been determined.
        if states[prevCat][prevMouse][prevMove]:
          continue
        if (prevMove == 0 and state == int(State.MOUSE_WIN) or
                prevMove == 1 and state == int(State.CAT_WIN)):
          states[prevCat][prevMouse][prevMove] = state
          q.append((prevCat, prevMouse, prevMove, state))
        else:
          outDegree[prevCat][prevMouse][prevMove] -= 1
          if outDegree[prevCat][prevMouse][prevMove] == 0:
            states[prevCat][prevMouse][prevMove] = state
            q.append((prevCat, prevMouse, prevMove, state))

    return states[2][1][0]

class Solution:
  def maxSubarraySumCircular(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
    totalSum = 0
    currMaxSum = 0
    currMinSum = 0
    maxSum = -math.inf
    minSum = math.inf

    for num in nums:
      totalSum += num
      currMaxSum = max(currMaxSum + num, num)
      currMinSum = min(currMinSum + num, num)
      maxSum = max(maxSum, currMaxSum)
      minSum = min(minSum, currMinSum)

    return maxSum if maxSum < 0 else max(maxSum, totalSum - minSum)

class Solution:
  def movesToStamp(self, stamp: str, target: str) -> list[int]:
    def stampify(s: int) -> int:
      """
      Stamps target[i..i + |stamp|) and returns the number of newly stamped
      characters.
      e.g. stampify("abc", "ababc", 2) returns 3 because target becomes "ab***".
      """
      stampified = len(stamp)

      for i, st in enumerate(stamp):
        if target[s + i] == '*':  # It's already been stamped.
          stampified -= 1
        elif target[s + i] != st:  # We can't stamp on the index i.
          return 0

      for i in range(s, s + len(stamp)):
        target[i] = '*'

      return stampified

    ans = []
    target = list(target)
    # stamped[i] := True if we already stamped target by stamping on index i
    stamped = [False] * len(target)
    stampedCount = 0  # Our goal is to make stampedCount = |target|.

    while stampedCount < len(target):
      isStamped = False
      # Try to stamp target[i..i + |stamp|) for each index.
      for i in range(len(target) - len(stamp) + 1):
        if stamped[i]:
          continue
        stampified = stampify(i)
        if stampified == 0:
          continue
        stampedCount += stampified
        isStamped = True
        stamped[i] = True
        ans.append(i)
      # After trying to stamp on each index, we can't find a valid stamp.
      if not isStamped:
        return []

    return ans[::-1]
